redVitalia: **Adaptar:** una acción principal inequívoca como “Agenda”, manteniendo una sola ruta dominante por landing.
**Copiar:** responder objeciones de precio, plazo, permanencia y resultados antes del CTA de alto compromiso.
**Probar:** WhatsApp como vía rápida, con consentimiento, SLA de respuesta y trazabilidad en CRM.
**Replicar la disciplina de medición:** el stack público detectado (WhatsApp) indica una captación instrumentada; RedVitalia debe mantener atribución de fuente a venta.

message.headline: Fill the calendar while saving prospecting time
message.promise: Automate lead discovery, scoring, WhatsApp outreach, follow-up and meeting booking in one product.
message.positioning: Kaptto sells an always-on prospecting product as a lower-cost alternative to manual SDR work.
message.audience: Small and medium B2B teams · Users willing to connect WhatsApp · Teams wanting a self-service prospecting workflow

forms.friction: The trial starts only after a payment card is added.

funnel.detail: The homepage emphasizes calendar outcomes, saved time and cost versus an SDR.
The visitor creates an account with Google or work credentials.
A seven-day card trial starts when payment details are added.
The user defines company, ICP, tone and goal, then connects WhatsApp.
Public CNPJ and Google Places data are enriched and scored with Gemini.
WhatsApp messages and follow-ups aim to book Google Calendar and Meet appointments.
Meeting context and performance data are presented in the product.

pricing: Starter: R$147 per month, 200 leads, 500 messages, 30 meetings and 3 niches
Pro: R$397 per month, 1,000 leads, 3,000 messages, 100 meetings and 10 niches
Enterprise: custom, up to 5,000 leads, 15,000 messages and unlimited meetings
Pix: R$137 or R$347 for 30 days, without trial or renewal
contract: Seven-day card trial begins when a card is added
Cancel before trial end to avoid charge
No proportional refund after seven days except stated service or billing cases
guarantee: No result guarantee; a seven-day payment refund policy applies under its stated conditions.

proof: Ratings shown within the brand experience
contradictions: cta-friction — The extra route change weakens an otherwise product-led journey. — The primary CTA says to start free. — The unauthenticated onboarding route first landed on login and required a separate signup choice.

outcome-qualification — Product capability should not be presented as an assured business outcome. — The product emphasizes booked meetings and a full calendar. — Terms disclaim guaranteed results, sales, conversion, data accuracy and integration continuity.
payment-modality — Trial messaging must be payment-method specific. — A seven-day trial reduces adoption friction. — Pix purchases have no trial and no renewal.
inferences: Transparent low pricing is intended to expand the category beyond agency buyers. — confidence: high — basis: The product is compared with a fraction of an SDR and exposes entry-level plans.
Card-gated trial balances product-led acquisition with payment intent. — confidence: medium — basis: Registration is free, but the actual seven-day trial begins when a card is added.
limitations: No card or WhatsApp account was connected.
Product performance and testimonial claims were not independently audited.

copy: Show every system integration in the workflow
Separate card trial and one-off payment conditions
Demonstrate product value before a sales call
avoid: A start-free CTA that lands on login
Implying outcome guarantees that terms explicitly reject
Displaying ratings without clear third-party provenance
test: Signup route with one unambiguous free-trial explanation
